body: My “other half” of urban tusa-jusa in Colombo has flowed smoothly into Weligama’s beach relaxation. The latter is a town on the southern tip of the island, administratively part of Matara District in the Southern Province. Judging by the number of people (and there were well a lot of homo sapiens distinctly untitled guise in addition to seven tens of thousands of local people), the "sand village" (which is how the name of the town translates to "native aspen language") is very popular as a place to relax among travelers from all over the globe. And one of the main "gravitation points" of the city, which is a remarkably harmonious combination of fishing village and beach resort - of course, the Weligama Beach here. To be honest, I didn't think these three kilometres of fine and clean sand were surfers' favourite spots (the latter, from personal experience, were associated exclusively with the beaches of Costa Adeje, Playa de las Americas, Los Cristianos), but it turned out to be just that!!! Not a day did I not see a dozen desperately sporty boys and girls bravely “saddle up” their boards and defy the waves of the Viligam coast. But in addition to these failed heroes of imperishable Catherine Bigelow's Point Break, there were even more less sporty traveller-beachphiles along the coastline who appreciated the virtues of Weligama Beach in their own way: a calm beach area, fine light sand, a light refreshing breeze, a beautiful posterior reefless set, clear Indian Ocean water... And add to this chic views with spreading palm trees - here and lovers of beautiful beach-sea photo shoots have a place to unfold in all its glory!!! And along the beach is full of affordable price tags and just "mind eat" delicious cooking restaurants and cafes for any taste. And if you are also a “remote freelancer” - a rousing morning swim, smoothly flowing into work under the shadow of one of the coffee shops, you are provided. We were in March and the only “minus” of the Giant beach was that at 11 o’clock it was time to return to the shade of the apartments or at least the palm leaves “umbrella” - the sun here by noon is already roasting undecky and the SPF 50+ cream is weakly saving. But in the evening, as the “lightbulb” of the sky luminary gradually goes over the horizon and evening freshness descends on Veligama, as the varanhas clamber into the bush and the hooligan monkeys begin to tuck into the bed somewhere there, on the “second floor” of the bush, in the “sand village” the time for romance, love and other pleasures of Sri Lankan holiday begins... Don't miss it!!!
title: Three kilometers of sand village coastline for beach relaxers

body: Weligam is actually a surfer, and that's where they went. Beautiful waves, gentle, long entrance. Clean water. I remember in Bali the first time I went into the water in Kut, wading through all the rubbish in the water before the waves formed. And here's the cleanest water, with a comfortable sandy bottom, and a little bit of sand clouding towards the shore, but not a single litter, equipped with surf school beds.Surf schools are located along the entire length of the beach, which first hold introductory theoretical classes, later warm-ups and then, accompanied by a coach, launch into the ocean)Well, it's obviously not suitable for swimming. body: The November rains in Weligama are creating a trash buildup in the ocean waters. I implore the government of Sri Lanka, hotels, surf camps, tourists, and local citizens to come together and make change. How does trash get into the ocean? Litter from streets and beaches carried by wind or rain, improper disposal washes into storm drains, rivers, and improper disposal from boats. What can we do to make change? Reduce single use plastics, recycle, support local legislation to decrease production of plastics, encourage use of reusable compostable non plastic bottles and bags, provide bins to dispose of trash properly, government dispose of trash in environmentally safe ways, spread the news, educate, volunteer and support charities who are trying to make change. I am a swimmer and bodysurfer and due to the trash in the ocean I do not recommend Weligama Beach. I spoke to managers at Weligama Marriott and Kai Beach Club. I am hoping there will be change from the top government and those with financial power, if not tourists will stop coming. I know I will not be returning.
title: Trash Dump Weligama Beach , Sri Lanka

body: We were staying at the Weligama Spa Hotel next to the Marriot. Outside our hotel on the beach was the cleanest. Came back and then walked in the other direction where there are surfers shacks and some eating places all along. Again not the cleanest and lots of sandbags, loose debris and broken slabs lying around and not the easiest to walk up to the road behind? It seemed to me that its really a place for young back packers. Though from the Mariott and our hotel there were lots of families with young children learning to surf and enjoy themselves. body: Weligama beach is large so it rarely feels too crowded. There's plenty of space on the beach itself, and in the water. There are no rocks or reefs either so its relatively safe for surfing. The only problem is the litter and local water pollution. After a day of swimming my shorts are brown from all the dirt in the water. If you go swimming, you'll feel plastic moving around near your feet (especially after heavy rains). There is next to no underwater visibility. So for swimming or snorkelling, you just need to get a Tuk Tuk to one of the many other nice beaches in the area. But for beginner or intermediate surfers its the best spot in the area.
title: Perfect for learning to surf

body: What can I say about Weligma. There's about 50 surf schools all. Down the beach where you can rent boards and get lessons.You can surf from 5.30amto 6.30 pm in small gentle waves. The afternoon is choppy. The line up is extremely busy all the time so that kind of sucks a lot. There are loads of European idiots who for some reason want to swim in front of begginer surfers who can't turn as they are learners....The fisherman are polite enough and there is loads of mangy dogs which sometimes run at you but are usually friendly enough. The worst thing that happened was when I went for a quick swim in between lessons a local man came and very obviously masturbated in front of me. The tuk tuks here are extremely annoying and forward and there are too many of them for the amount of travellers. I recommend for beginners for 4-7 days get some lessons but you get sick of the place after that. Or for advanced surfers who want to challenge themselves by dodging between 50 learners. The shops and restaurants on the main road are way more expensive too. If you are confident walk in a few streets and get a local meal. It's quite a tourist trap. I was there for twelve days, but had I the choice in would have left in 5.
title: Good learner surf, very busy

body: If you're looking for a place away from the hustle and bustle of Mirissa and the main Weligama beach area go to this beautiful quiet spot and enjoy the peace, swimming, surfing, beds to lay on and order delicious foods and drinks from the Grand Beach Restaurant where this lovely family spoil you with their dishes.

body: Consistent low to medium waves all through the day, combined with loads of surf schools and capable instructors make this beach ideal for learning basic surfing skills. Beach is clean and sand is soft.

body: The surfing in Weligama was the best ever, our whole family enjoyed the gentle waves and there was plenty of space, never felt crowded. The water was warm and nice. Will definitely come back on next surf trip with the family

body: Had a lovely time learning to surf here. There is a vegan nicecream van along the beach edge so I enjoyed a lesson and a dairy free / sugar free / gluten free treat afterwards. The guys at the surf board stands are super helpful and friendly. Plenty of sun beds to choose from when resting after your dip. The water does get very busy with surfers and it’s for beginners only as you can only go straight on a wave. If you try go left or right when it’s busy you are going to crash into others. There are many other surf spots near by for intermediate at Jungle beach for long board surfers and further along 10mins away for short board surfing at coconut beach. Fun and safe place to stay! Plenty of little shops also. For both surf gear and jewellery.
title: Great town to surf, eat and shop for jewellery!

body: best for surf beginners there are a lot of cafes hostels hotels and surf schools.Try different places also i reccommend night fish market

body: We visited Weligama Beach when taking our son for a surf lesson and thought it was one of the best in our Sri Lanka vacation.Set on a wide bay, the water is warm and clear, the beach is broad and welcoming and the surf conditions were ideal for lessons.It is busy, full of surfers of all levels, and occasionally tricky to navigate because of it. body: Unfortunately we found Weligama bay dirty, polluted, littered with plastic and neglected. Sad to see after enjoying wonderful beaches along the south coast. They will give you much better prices and also take lots of care to help you progress.
title: Fantasitic beach to learn to surf

body: It's the most lively place in Waligama, completely safe for surfing. Locals are very friendly and welcoming the tourists.
title: Safe and lively place

body: The bay is amazing! With golden sands and a long stretch of beach, this is also a great spot for surfing judging by the dozens dotting the water on all sides.
title: Beautiful bay

body: Vast beachline with surf schools and other water activities, cafes and restaurants. Amazing sunsets, sometimes parties at night. Great for surf beginners as the bay has a sand bottom therefore more safe. Not quite that great for swimming especially for kids, because of big waves and surf beginners.
title: Weligama bay beach

body: Fantastic beach, beautiful views and great sunset, many surfers and an unreal atmosphere. I Loving it!
title: Fantastic beach

body: Great beach with very good crowd. Nice people stay in that area too. I am not a surfer - everyone there is surfing but I enjoyed the waves as they were not that crazy. Food and refreshments in that area are also affordable with a good variety. I loved the atmosphere. Fishermen start their journeys here too.
title: Clean, beautiful beach!

body: Super nice surfer location in south cost. fisher mans also working any time on the beach. nice sunsets. but not clean
title: super nice

body: Being slightly sheltered in the bay, the waves here can be cleaner and smaller than other parts of the coast. It's a great place for the family to sit, hire a board and enjoy the beach. Great spot to spend a few hours.
title: Great beach to hire a board and get a few waves!

body: The beach is very dirty and polluted and the surrounding area feels very run down. We planned to spend a day here but left at midday to go back to Mirissa as the beach is much nicer.
title: Run down

body: Stayed at the hotel fir 3 nights and ate in the restaurant every night as the service and food was great.
title: Lovely setting

body: This is a good beach for walk or to just hangout. The waves are strong and high,this time it's not recommended to get into water.
title: Waves

body: My boyfriend had some surfing lessons from which the price afterwards got more expensive... So watch out for: ‘oni surf lessons’. They will come up to you when you are on the beach. Try one of the good rated ones on TripAdvisor instead.The beach itself was filled with sandflies. I’m still very very itchy:(
title: Surfing ok, beach filled with sandflies

body: Weligama beach is a treu beauty. Special the bay. At the beach you can find surf schools so you can learn to surf just in one day. So beautiful and can never get enough of this clean blue water. ❤️
title: Beauty

body: Be cool surf.....avoid at all cost. These are bullying scammers. They will fake damage to your hired surf board and demand ridiculous amounts of money and get aggressive.
title: Scammers

body: Constant waves for beginners, the beach is huge too so no worries about overcrowding. A few restaurants here and there. Worth a visit for an afternoon!
title: Nice beach for surfing

body: Definitely worth a visit if you are a surf enthusiast. many surf schools located on the beach and even if you are just looking to get some tan lines and a good swim this is the place to be. Many nice little cafe's along the Galle road and it's not hard to score a place to stay here.
title: Best Place for Beginners to learn surf.

body: We stayed in one of the hotels that faced the Beach, and we were surprised how quiet is was considering we were travelling in late March. It is a little busier at the Marriot Hotel end, which stands out like a sore thumb and is not in character with the area as a whole. A small amount of cafes operate in the evening on the beach for meals and drinks, which is a nice experience. Good for novice surfers too, plus a warm sea which is never cold. The reason would not award it five stars is mainly the rubbish (plastic) that is brought in around the fishing boat area. We saw a sea turtle that had died which is likely due to getting plastic into its body. There is no urgency to clean it up and that is a concern.
title: Lovely Quiet Beach

body: This is a very touristy beach. Which is just full of beach culture. There are learn to surf schools and surfboard hire shops every where you look. There are plenty of vegetarian eateries to choose from and if your into yoga this is the place to be. It is a very picturesque beach.
title: Wide Stretch Of Beach

body: not steep beginning sea but further on possible to surf even at evenibg while lighted .Some fisherboats also on the beach .Sunset advised.Along a boulevard with cafe and restaurants at the town site and shadow at the beachside
title: broad beach close to city eating on the beach

body: The ocean was like bath water, the beach was smooth and sandy. Lots of surfers out on the waves. Enjoyed the area, walking around to the town, experiencing Sri Lanka. We'll return.
title: Beautiful sandy beach

body: This beach is great for surf beginners, waves are not that big and moreover there are many surf schools that rent surf boards for half the price than at the Mirissa beach.
title: Great for surf beginners

body: It was my first time I did surfing, it's amazing, people here are doing surfing, so not suitable for swimming, if you want to have a great time surfing, come here..
title: Best place for surfing

body: One of main surfing points in Sr Lanka. Large sandy beach area. Very crowded during December to April. Facing to Galle-Matara highway. Therefore easy access.
title: Lot of attractions

body: We walked along this beach maybe two km, it could be a lovely beach, but loads of rubbish, particularly plastic, also lots of dogs, we saw nothing to suggest this is a beauty spot but can see that the surf is good for beginners.
title: Filthy and loads of rubbish

body: Perfect place for surf beginners! Not too clan because of alltime waves - but warm, quiet and very beautiful
title: Great for surf beginners

body: Clean blue sea with steady waves. It is a surfers paradise with plenty of shops around to help you learn surfing. For others who just want to enjoy the sea, it offers plenty of opportunities as well
title: Surfers Paradise

body: This beach is for those who want to surf, relax or soak up the local atmosphere. We stayed up the quiet end of the beach but walked along the beach into the town, this was a nice walk. The local bars are a must at night..... Grab a cocktail during happy hour.
title: Great Beach

body: There are MANY surf schools set up in the centre of the beach, which can make it feel a little busy in the water if you just want to swim. However, it’s a beautiful long beach & we enjoyed walking along the sand to find more space to swim. One of my favourite beaches in Sri Lanka!
title: Beautiful, long, sandy beach

body: Amazing place to surf and best to learn surf. This time we did a photography tour for a Israel team at Weligama and that was amazing experience. (This is 4th year,before Arugambay & Kabalana) This is a Amazing place to stay, relax, eat, surf.. Lot of people wanted us there, unfortunately we had to leave the place in 4 days as we had willpattu safari tour with some other team. If anyone want join with us at weligama, pls write us.
title: 🏄 Surfing Photography Tour..

body: Perfect beach for young families and beginning surfers. Lots of surf lessons and people enjoying the ocean.
title: Wide and safe Beach

body: One of the best in Sri Lanka.Good for surfers.Long for relaxing walk.Sea great and warm.Relaxing.
title: Exellent

body: Beach is clean and water is clear. The waves there is suitable for surf beginner. However, there is not much shop or store there which made dining option is limited.
title: Nice clean beach

body: If you are in downsouth , this is a place to get a bath . Beautiful views and many good restaurants . A perfect place to spend an evening.
title: Beautiful Weligama bay

body: Perfect place for surfing both for beginners and advanced. Sandy beach, boards for rent ( 2500 rupees per hour). The guys clean it every morning but I wish they do that better. A bit smells fish
title: For surfing

body: Very beautiful sea waves and also sea windy of indian ocien of south coast of beautiful sri lanka.i love this place.
title: Sea shells

body: I don't understand how can the people surf and swim on this beach, the water is polluted and smelly. You can see all the pollution from the city going to the water. Incredible how we can see people inside with so many fantastic beaches in sri Lanka.
title: Polluted beach

body: As a swimmer it's a little bit stressful as surfers think they own the place...(they do). Clean enough in front of hotels but Weligama could do more to keep it clean as they are getting enough tourist money in to pay someone to clean it up once a day at low tide.
title: Surf city

body: Weligama Beach isn’t anything to write home about to be honest. It’s very shabby. The fisherman treat the beach like a rubbish tip, locals should take care of the place otherwise word will get out it’s nothing special. I was disappointed.
title: Underwhelming Beach

body: Great for surfing and swimming. No sellers or harrassment....Only a few restaurants and facilities, but its really nice here
title: Excellent Beach

body: Weligama beach is a very good spot for surfing from beginner to intermediates. Perfevt if you have never touched a board, in 30 min a teacher will put you on a wave for less than 20 dollars and then it will be on you. Renting is as cheap as 3 dollar per hour. Sunsets are beautiful, watch it enjoying a coconut or a mango lassi
title: Great for surf

body: Yes, a great spot for beginner surfers which is evident by the number of boards bobbing about in the water. However, the water is quite sandy from the way the waves roll in. If you're expecting clear waters and a beach to laze about on, head further along the coast.
title: Surf Don't Swim

body: Good beach to take a walk. Not sandy, not good for strolling. Can take bath, waves a gentle. No place to sit though. Primarily used for learning surfing. Rs. 2000 for 90 minute lesson.
title: Bath or learn surfing

body: Very well maintained. The actually fishing boats are a real bonus. There are surfing lessons available.
title: Calm Waters, clean beaches

body: We visited Weligama Beach after Mirissa and were disappointed by the amount of rubbish everywhere. We went for dinner on the beach and were surrounded by crows. My girlfriend got an upset stomach probably from the water. The beautiful beaches of Sri Lanka are going to be destroyed by plastic waste if something isn’t done soon.
title: Full of litter, crows and sand flies

body: Beautiful calm and clean beach stretch with lots of restaurants and accommodation providing places close by. I saw some outlets were offering surfing and snorkeling lessons there.
title: Great for wind surfing or swimming / snorkeling

body: This beach thrives only on surfers and families with small kids. Shallow water really far out from the beach so you can basically stand on the bottom and fall onto your board for the surf. The beach itself is packed with cheep surf schools and board rentals. A few beach side hotels exist, out of which two account for all the music played from lunch to midnight. The large Marriott resort totally destroys the chill and nice vibe although surely makes the place more suitable for families and older couples. Almost no activity on the beach during evenings in regards of restaurants and such (except around the resorts).
title: Surfing. And surfing Only.

body: Nice vibe full of young people, good for surfing and chilling and watching the sunset :)Not so good for swimming and many sand flies which bite a lot :(
title: Good for surfing and sunset but many sand flies

body: Weligama beach is probably the largest surf bay on the south east of the island. It’s a shallow sand reef which make it safe although the waves are moving quite a bit. For an advanced surfer it’s probably crap but for beginners/intermediate surfers it’s a heaven, perfect for longboarding and training and learning since the waves seldom is higher than 4 ft and comes quite slowly. And thanks to the conditions the bay is packed with surf schools and surf hotels and as a result of that the water is sometimes overcrowded. Not many of the surfers would be certified in “surf etiquette” so there are quite often accidents. It has a nice wibe though with new cool places like Ceylon Sliders and W15 and will probably be really hip in the coming years.
title: Crowded beginners/intermediate heaven

body: Great spot, white sand, constant waves for surfing, loads of surf schools... great for singles, families and couples... fun for everyone
title: Lovely beach with bars/restaurants

body: If you're traveling through Sri Lanka and would like to try how it works on a surfboard you should go for a visit to Weligama Beach. There are plenty of surf schools where you just can go and ask for a surf lesson. Very wide and nice beach.
title: Very nice beach for surfers

body: This is an amazing beach. We stayed at the Weligama Marriot hotel I would highly recommend and rate as one of Sri Lanka’s best hotels. The beach has amazingly soft shaft and generally very clean and safe for locals and foreigners alike. The waves aren’t too harsh that the kids too enjoyed. Right in front of the hotel there a guys renting surf and boday boards. Veranga has two jet skis and is super friendly and takes you on rides for a fee and if your confident enough will allow you to take it out yourself. Note worthy is Veranga and his friends on the beach clean the beach spotless of all the garbage and plastic that floats in. They are supported by the hotel who helps to discharge the collected debris. What’s amazing is that they are not paid for this service but genuinely do it out of pure love for the beach. One can contact Veranga on (077) 173 2614 if required.
title: Best beach

body: Amazing beach great if you love to surf and plenty of people to teach you if you can’t but also great to just relax or swim lots or cafes to eat in aw well
title: Chill out time

body: So special to swim in the Indian Ocean from such a beautiful, convenient and picturesque beach. Worth a visit.
title: Great beach

body: Lovely beach but be careful spending too much time in the water, particularly up by the island. Ear infections and stomach bugs are common due to the filthy water that flows out of the river there.
title: Nice beach but the water is filthy

body: I was at the Weligama Beach in Weligama for a few days in February. I was staying at the near by Ahangama, and it was the closest popular beach to my hotel. The beach is very beautiful, great sunsets over here, and some fantastic beach shacks. It is a very popular beach with surfers. The only thing to be careful about is that the water currents here are strong and can pull you in. So please be careful when you go in the sea, it can be dangerous despite the life guard presence.
title: Beautiful, but be careful

body: I originally from Weligama, so I know this is one of the best beach you can find in Southern Coastal to enjoy your day. When you come to the beach you can see the whole Weligama Bay and if you like you can enjoy the sunrise as well as sunset in this beach because both scenery add extra beauty to Weligama Beach.
title: Great Beach For relaxing, sports and chilling.

body: The beach next to Fisherman's Bay Hotel is very quiet and is an excellent location for bathing. It is well covered with a reef as such the water is calm and is safe for even small children. There are a lot of fishing boats anchored around the place and the water is shallow. The sun goes down by 5pm and there is not much crowd in this part of the bay as it is mostly used by the guests of Fisherman's Bay hotel.
title: Weligama Bay Beach

body: Lovely white sand palm trees and aqua blue water. Only thing I didn't like was in some parts there was quite a lot of litter in the scrubland.
title: Beautiful Sri Lankan Beach

body: Huge beach with pretty clean sand, not too bad waves and excellent sunsets. Nice to walk along the strand line - not too much plastic.
title: Wonderful beach

body: Learnt to Surf on this beach. Beach had endless waves rolling in. Lucky our surf instructor from the Lions Rest Hotel was awsome. Boards on top of the Tuk Tuk.There are a number of surf schools along the beach. Waves were great.
title: Surfing Holiday

body: We stayed at the Marriott and had a beautiful view of the whole bay. Its a lovely beach for strolling in the shallows and seems reasonable clean in most parts.
title: Beautiful bay

body: Here's some facts about the beach. It's a safe beach, where the waves are perfect PERFECT for surfers of all levels.There are shacks aplenty where the "Surfing Boys" base themselves and they are looking for your business.Note: If you a beginner surfer and want a board only, choose one with one fin, not three. You are likely to loose one in the surf and they will charge you for it. They know this, you probably should in advance. To avoid "hidden" extra costs go with a surfing lesson.The sand is white and in places clean. In others it is scattered with dead fish. There are a few restaurants overlooking the beach and sea, but not many.The water is so very warm.At night time towards the end of the beach where the Marriott Hotel is massive night lights come on, pointing out to sea allowing for night surfing.A thought has to go out to the devastating tsunami wave which once took out this beach and everything close by.It's a HUGE beach and maybe that's why it doesn't rate for non-surfer me as a beach to sit or swim at for any great length of time. For me it just didn't have that more intimate, idyllic feel to it. Thankfully there are lots of beaches like this in close vicinity so you can pick and choose depending on how you feel if you base yourself at Weligama.
title: Come To Weligama As A Great Base, But Not For Beach Only - Unless You're A Surfer

body: We Stayed at the Marriott, amazing beach, so clean and so little people, it feels as though the beach is all yours.
title: Beautiful Beach!

body: Crescent shaped idelic and quiet beach that has wide expanse of beach area for quiet walks in the early morning or late evening to experience the gentle and rhythmic beauty of the ocean waves.
title: Idelic and quiet beach

body: Really nice beach. Not at all crowded and you will find surfing teachers and instructors available for a little fee. I found the beach to be clean. While not a clear beach, the white water waves are nice and debris free. Opportunities exist for jet ski, surfing 🏄‍♀️
title: Lovely beach with a view of the sunset

body: It’s a great beach for surfing and you can go for a nice run along the beach. I saw some turtles hatch which was a big u expected surprise. If you stay at Surf N Lanka the guys can not only teach you how to surf but also teach you how to play cricket!
title: Nice beach

body: The beach is a beautiful beach to swim at. The water was beautiful and clear and warm. Do yourself a favour and come here
title: BEAUTIFUL BEACH

body: This is a nice beach but there is basically no shade on this beach, be cautious of the hot sun! The waves are sometimes rough so be careful with that too..
title: Nice beach

body: Weligama Beach was much quieter than going to Mirissa or Una. It isn't lined thickly with restaurants and bars. We rented some surf boards and got a 2 hour lesson, it was a good beach to learn to surf in and the guys who gave us the lesson were really great and patient with us. We were a group of 10 and they were awesome to pay attention to all us. I liked this beach very much,
title: Quieter place to be

body: A clean beach very popular with surf boarders, especially beginners at this time of the year. Plenty of sufing schools with qualified teachers dotting the shore. A great place to relax with a beer (there are small restaurants serving it right by the beach). Two areas are demarcated for parking of colourful fishing catamarans.
title: Surf's up

body: Lovely beach for walking and night life. Lots of bars and sea food restaurants. Surf clubs plenty. Safe for children.
title: Bathing and surfing

body: Very expansive clean beach particularly the Beach front of Marriot Hotel. Ideal for surfing and swimming.Fishing boats too can be observed as an added experience. Ideal times morning or towards evening.
title: Super Beach

body: The Weligama beach is a great place where you can learn to surf. At the beach a lot of small surfing schools and places to rent surf board and other equipment. There were not a lot of people swimming in the ocean, I suppose because of the surfers. The beach is for sure a place to visit.
title: Nice place)

body: Was dissapointed by merissa so moved on to weligama beach and it wasn't much better, reminded me of kuta beach with lots of hawkers, pop up bars and surf schools. But less physical distance between the sea and road to fit it all in. The sea was in and it had swept all the trash from these places into the sea. I saw paint pots, wood pallets and metal sheet in the water. The beautiful images you see of this beach on the internet muat be very old as there is now a marriot hotel that looks like an inner city apartment block and lots of rubbish running along it's length.
title: Trashed and ruined

body: Escape the hassle and hustle of Mirissa and walk along Weligambay beach. This is definitely a better experience and nobody hassles you here.Just take your time to enjoy a walk or a swim. After all, you're on holiday..?
title: Soft, white sand

body: The water is super warm and the sand felt so soft under my feet. Beach offers surfboard rentals and lessons. The waves are perfect for surfing and swimming never rough. There are some wild dogs on the beach they are super friendly and love affection and maybe a treat ;)
title: Beautiful, Clean and Safe.

body: Great surf spot for beginners. Most of the people do one-off lessons but some shops have surf camps as well.
title: Great surf spot for beginners.

body: A lovely long, flat, walking beach that is still has a fishing village feel despite the multitude of surfing schools. At the western end is Fish point with all it's stalls and restaurants.
title: A Working Beach

body: this beach is perfect for surfing, but less good for the relax, better beach for relax you can find in MIrissa
title: nice quite beach

body: Must visit! Options for water sports and surfing are plenty.There are sea view hotels that you can check into. It's worth.
title: Clean beautiful beach

body: great for surfing. has some high end hotels and clubs right on the beach. it is less busy then Melissa
title: lovely beach

body: Big beach with lots of surf schools and surf rental places on the beach. Good place for learning to surf.
title: Big beach

body: The Weligama beach is ideal for families and we spent a lot of time on the beach and in the water. The surf is relatively gentle and the water is not very deep.
title: Great beach

body: Nice quite beach, where is many beginners for surfing, small waves. Not so many hotels, some small "restaurants" and great restaurant in small hotel Weligama Bay Resort (not in Marriott).
title: Nice quite beach

body: The waves here makes it a good place for learners. Its a very calm and cozy sea, nice flat bed white sand.
title: A surfer's paradise

body: This is a big open beach with surf good for beginners. One end of the beach has pretty boats and emerald water - great photos.
title: Pretty beach for beginner surfers

body: The beach stretches off from the town for several km. The area near the town is cluttered, first with fish restaurants, then with a ridiculous number of wall-to-wall gazebo "surf schools", and finally the hideous slab of the Marriott - all of this new since I last visited in 2011, when it was quiet and delightful.. Get beyond all that though and there's always a pleasant breeze to keep you cool. I don't surf but the bay is level, shallow and sandy, great for swimming, even for small children. Also down this far end of the beach are some pleasant out-of-town guesthouses with beach access, so have a wander and see if anything appeals.
title: A long sandy beach, pleasant for a walk

body: Best surf school at Weligama beach! Heshan is the teacher/owner of One Love Surf Camp. A very friendly, relaxed and good teacher! We highly recommend this surf school. He taught us the basics of surfing. Very reliable and good surf school (fair prices)!
title: One Love Surf Camp!

body: One of the great beaches in Sri lanka to surf .. Highly recommend for a beginner who likes to surf as the waves of this place is a good start for you to learn surfing .... i recommend love bar surf camp a guy call Heshan was the one who teached me and ever since i met him i have taken many of my foreign friends .. A very good teacher and a very friendly person ... however if you want to take a dip i recommend you to stay in the shallow and not go too deep as the current can get a bit strong .... a very relaxed beach with beautiful people around .... a chill beer in the evening is highly recommended
title: Surf school

body: Welligamma beach is a nice clean area which allows for easy swimming and is popular with surfers. Some fishing boats and fisherman may be viewed launching their vessels and their catches at early morning. A nice walk to a small private island which is now a very exsclive bed and breakfast venue.
title: Our visit

body: A lovely long stretch of beach with many surf shacks and schools along its length. Plenty of snack bars too, and local fishermen to watch the time slip away whilst enjoying a Lion beer!
title: Great beach and plenty of surfing

body: I like this place. It´s calm, mostly it´s clean and most important - there are waves which you can surf on anytime all day! I spent here 10 days recently and now Im only thinking how to get back:) Im givin only 4/5 because sometimes the beach can be dirty after the rain or at "non touristic" areas.
title: Nice place, great fort Surf beginners

body: We came to Weligama beach for sea bath..Its a safety plase for swimming and surfing.There are low price rooms to stay.
title: Beautiful Beach

body: Awesome beach .... it's been overtaken a bit by the European style of using beach sun beds and it was a bit difficult to find a square inch to out a towel on the sand and it has been inundated by a ridiculous amount of surf schools, however the beach and the water itself were lovely. Just be a bit careful as there is no separate area for swimming (unlike most areas of the world) and you are constantly watching out that a surf board doesn't take your head off... there are however nice swimming beaches close by that are more secluded ... it's just a shame because the bay beach is really lovely
title: Great beach

body: Would stay here though if I don't need to be close to surf. No restaurants along the beach like in Mirissa that has SO much better atmosphere....
title: Boring as a beach but great for beginner surfing!

body: There are lots of Surf Schools along this beach which is a superb venue for beginners to learn to surf.
title: Great surfing beach for beginners

body: A lovely long beach with surfable but not punishing waves. Lots of surf schools. Sand that goes a long way out, so you can recover after your repeated falls. This has to be the easiest place to learn to surf.
title: The best place to learn to surf.

body: Beach has something for everyone party central on one side and quiet family accommodation on the other.
title: Nice beach decent surf

body: We stayed in a villa directly on Weligama Beach which was fantastic. Beach was pretty clean for Sri Lanka and not too busy. Surfers mainly out first thing in morning and late in evening. We did find that you had to avoid some pollution at certain times of day, but this was easy to do by just going further down beach. There were a lot of stray dogs but they do not bother you if you ignore them - although do not leave your stuff unattended or they will pee on it!
title: Lovely Beach

body: Watch the sun rise / set its like something out of a movie,Sit relax with friends or family enjoy a fresh cut coconut milk drink ,an ice cold lion beer, what more could you want ?.
title: Beautiful beach

body: this beach is near to main road..its in curve shape half moon type shape.. we didn't bath here.. but at evening time its nice..one can see the beach from road, at night candle light dinner being arranged from local restaurants which are situated on beach. I saw many people surf here..too
title: diffrent than ordinary beach

body: Stopped here to see the Stilt Fishermen in the waves. Nice sunset ocean views along the beach during our visit.
title: Nice sunset ocean views

body: Pretty easy to get there by bus or tuk. Situated in the weligama Bay. Clean beach with little waves. Few surf schools are there. Better to check the equipments before renting. Lots of restaurants and affordable price. There is a small island called taprobane island. Looks awesome when the sun is setting. Can have a peaceful evening beach walk.
title: Less crowded peaceful beach.

body: Took a day trip over from Mirissa, much calmer seas here, lots of surfers, had a great lunch at the catermaran truck restaurant parked on the seafront. Beach was great.
title: Wonderful beach

body: For surf beginners the waves are perfect. But if you are looking for some bigger waves, better go to the eastern part of the country. Evenmore, it is totally crowded, but a very beautiful beach.
title: small waves but beautiful beach

body: This was our favourite beach on Sri Lanka. Even if the beach was packed with surfers, it was shallow enough, so that we could let our eight-year-old jump around in the waves. Other beaches we visited, had deeper water, which made it impossible to leave him without supervision, but here he could jump around by himself. And the sunsets were spectacular.
title: Great beach for kids

body: We have been visiting Weligama for very many years and always enjoy walking along the golden sandy beach, listening to the waves of the Indian Ocean crashing against the shore. This beach is a lively place and is good for sunbathing, surfing, walking and bathing - though we advise anyone to be careful of tides and currents. There are numerous small surfing schools along the promenade adjacent to the beach and there are many restaurants and bars in the vicinity. The beach is fairly clean, though we have seen areas that are polluted. The various fishing vessels that park on the beach also add to the very pleasant atmosphere. Hotels are multiplying rapidly in this area and accommodation will not be difficult to find.
title: Beautiful sandy beach with plenty of activity

body: The beach is a protected harbor and great for learning how to surf. Lots of surf schools along the beach offering lessons and board rentals. Some parts were a little dirty but the parts by the hotels were always clean.
title: Great to learn to surf
One of Best Beaches in the south coast of Sri Lanka
body: During the season sea is clam and warm. Good beach area with plenty of space. Fairly clean. Surfing is very popular here. There are places where they teach surfing for the beginners.
